states: Private mock stack built from this tree (backend rebuilt at the base commit, Vite serving the edited sources): Alerts > Overview with 13 active mock alerts, one critical Docker service alert (ops-prometheus) and warnings, including the Acknowledged section and the Unacknowledge control on an acknowledged card.

Before the change (origin/main bea0cec8b9, same stack): after a local Acknowledge then a curl unacknowledge, /api/alerts/active reported acknowledged:false while the overview kept the card hidden and read '2 critical, Acknowledged 1' against a nav badge of 3 critical, until reload.

After the change at 1280x900 and 375x812: the same card returns to the active list as the first card within 2 seconds of the remote unacknowledge, the header counts agree with the nav badge, and no toast fires.

Socket-beats-response race (acknowledge response held 1.5s in the page so the broadcast lands first, then a server-side unacknowledge 200ms after it resolves): the card is back at once and no 'Server did not confirm' toast or REST re-fetch occurs over 18s. With only websocket.ts reverted to main, the card stayed hidden about 16s and then that toast fired.
Only console error on the final load is the existing 403 of the acknowledge request's first attempt, which the API client retries with a fresh CSRF token (same on main).
interactions: Clicked Acknowledge on the critical card, then POST /api/alerts/unacknowledge for that alert from curl (another session); repeated at both viewports.

Restore direction: curl acknowledge of a warning alert, clicked Unacknowledge in the tab (card returns to active, 'Alert restored' toast), then curl acknowledge again; the card moved back to Acknowledged within 2 seconds.
Race run driven from the page with a fetch wrapper delaying the acknowledge response and AlertsAPI.unacknowledge sent after it, watching toasts and /api/alerts/active requests.
